This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases v2.86-dev and v2.87-dev.

Most of this is security and maintenance. Nothing in the app looks or behaves
differently, with one exception worth reading before you update — see **Action
required** below if your servers sit behind a restrictive firewall or proxy.

## Security updates

- **Next.js updated to 16.3.4.** This is the important one. It closes two
  critical remote-code-execution advisories and around twenty further issues
  covering middleware/proxy bypasses, server-side request forgery, cache
  poisoning and denial of service. It also brings in patched versions of two
  bundled libraries that carried their own advisories.
- **The email library updated to nodemailer 10.** Fixes five advisories,
  including one that allowed a crafted message to read local files or make
  requests to internal addresses, and two that let a carefully-formed recipient
  address bypass domain checks. This affects scheduled exports delivered by
  email.
- **The spreadsheet engine now comes from the vendor's own site.** The copy on
  the public package registry has been frozen for years on a release with two
  known advisories (prototype pollution and a regular-expression denial of
  service), and no fix was ever published there. Training Tracker now installs a
  current, patched release directly from the vendor. Excel imports and exports
  are unchanged — same behaviour, same file formats.

Running an update now reports **no critical vulnerabilities** (previously one)
and **four high** (previously eight), with **two** deprecation notices instead of
three.

## Action required — only if you allow-list outbound hosts

Because of the spreadsheet change above, installs and updates now need outbound
HTTPS to **`cdn.sheetjs.com`** in addition to `registry.npmjs.org`. If your
firewall or proxy restricts which hosts the server can reach, **add it before
your next update** — otherwise the update will fail while installing that one
package. There is a note in the README's Troubleshooting section.

If your server has unrestricted outbound internet access, there is nothing to do.

## Under the hood

- **The codebase passes its own linter again.** Forty-four accumulated errors
  were fixed in the code itself — none were silenced or the rules relaxed.
- **Report pages now share the app's standard data-fetching hook.** The eight
  server-paginated reports each carried their own near-identical copy of the
  loading logic; they now share one implementation, along with the Training
  catalogue, Students list, Offerings dashboard, partner-program dashboard and
  the Backup file list.
- **Two latent bugs fixed.** The partner-program and offering dashboards could
  briefly show results for the wrong scope if you changed country or region
  while a slower request was still in flight. Both now discard superseded
  responses.
- **Add/Edit dialogs are created fresh each time they open** — the program
  requirement, program tier and offering requirement dialogs — instead of being
  kept open and reset by hand, so nothing can linger between openings.
- **Slightly better loading states.** Signing in and landing on a page now shows
  a loading state while your profile and company list load, rather than briefly
  rendering as though you were signed out.

## Also

- **Google API client updated**, which removes one of the three deprecation
  notices at its source.
- **Five unused packages removed** from the install. None were referenced
  anywhere in the app; they were left behind by earlier work and were being
  downloaded on every deployment for nothing. Installs are correspondingly
  smaller.
- **Automated checks now run on every change.** Linting and type-checking run on
  every push, and a release can no longer be created from code that fails
  either. This is what stopped the forty-four errors above from being noticed
  for so long.

## Known and deliberately left alone

Three items still appear during updates and are worth explaining rather than
hiding:

- **One of the two remaining deprecation notices** concerns a small helper
  package used deep inside the Google API client. It is a "this is built into
  modern Node.js now" notice, not a vulnerability, and it is present in every
  current version of that client — so there is nothing to upgrade to. Removing
  it would mean dropping the Google client entirely and hand-writing the Drive
  upload, which is not worth it for a cosmetic warning.
- **The code-linting tool stays on its current major version**, so its
  deprecation notice remains. The newer version exists, but three of the
  plug-ins our Next.js preset depends on have not been updated for it — one
  crashes outright on every file. This was tried and reverted rather than
  shipped broken. It is a development-time tool that is not part of the running
  application.
- **Four high-severity advisories remain**, all in the database toolkit's
  command-line tool. There is no fixed release on the version line we are on;
  the only available "fix" is a downgrade this app cannot take. It is a
  build-time tool rather than part of the running application, and the specific
  vulnerable component is a MySQL driver that a PostgreSQL app never loads. We
  will pick up the fix when the next major version of that toolkit ships.
